name: 80-Mesh Garnet Abrasive
notes: List price. ~2.75 hr of cutting per bucket at 0.33 lb/min. Ours has come through dealer orders (PDI) — WAZER recommends against third-party garnet.

name: WAZER Nozzle
notes: Wear item — replace when kerf widens or cuts taper.

name: Timink 712XL Ink Combo Pack (compatible)
notes: What we actually buy (Aug 2025 order). Third-party high-yield set for the DesignJet T630.

name: HP 712 80-ml Black Ink (genuine)
notes: Genuine HP option (paid $64.90 in 2022). Cyan/Magenta/Yellow 29-ml: 3ED67A/3ED68A/3ED69A.

name: 24" × 150' Bond Plotter Paper Roll
notes: Any 24" 20-lb bond with 2" core works. (List price — no receipt on file.)

name: Prismatic Powders PLUM RIVER (team purple)
notes: The signature purple — reordered 4+ times ($138.80 in 2024 → $147.10 in 2025). Store sealed with desiccant; moist powder spits.

name: Cricut StandardGrip Mat 12×12 (green)
notes: First set came in the Maker 4 Ultimate Bundle. LightGrip (blue) for paper, StrongGrip (purple) for thick materials.

name: Cricut Premium Fine-Point Blade + Housing
notes: Replacement blades only: 2007301 (2-pack).

name: HTV (Heat Transfer Vinyl) Rolls
notes: Cut mirrored, shiny side down. 305°F / 15 s / medium pressure.

name: Vinyl Transfer Tape
notes: Medium-tack for adhesive vinyl decals.

name: Anodized Aluminum Sublimation Sheets (custom 5251 H24)
notes: 14 custom sheets ordered Aug 2025 ($672 + $300 freight) for sublimation-on-metal signs.

name: 1/8" Aluminum Blind Rivets
notes: Restocked in McMaster orders (large-diameter domed head, 0.126–0.25" grip). Stock 3/16" too.

name: 3/16" Aluminum Large-Flange Blind Rivets
notes: Large flange spreads load on polycarb and soft materials (Mar 2026 order, ×2 boxes).

name: WCP Aluminum Nutstrip 6" (#10-32, 0.5" spacing)
notes: Bought 10 in Aug 2026 (order 26-52686). 10+ WCP orders in the 2026 season.

name: #10-32 BHCS Black Oxide (2.5" / 3")
location: Small parts wall, bolt bins by length
notes: The robot-standard fastener. Long lengths restocked Aug 2026.

name: External Retaining Rings 3/8" & 1/2"
notes: Black-phosphate spring steel, for hex shaft (Apr 2026 order 63139602).

name: M6 Nylon-Insert Locknuts
notes: Metric hardware for swerve/COTS assemblies.

name: 10:1 Epoxy Static Mixing Nozzles
notes: For 10:1 structural adhesive cartridges.

name: Clear Polycarbonate Tube 2" OD × 6 ft
notes: Bought 5 in Mar 2026 (20% promo). Zoro = our raw-stock vendor: free shipping + frequent 10–20% promo codes.

name: White Polypropylene Sheet 48"×48"×0.094"
notes: Used for bumper backing and liners (Apr 2026 order). Cuts cleanly on the bandsaw and jigsaw.

name: 20mm CO2 Laser Focus Lens
notes: Replacement focus lens — swap when cleaning no longer restores cut quality.

name: xTool MetalFab Cutting Nozzles
notes: Fiber laser cutting nozzle consumables (Mar 2026 order 415225).

name: Reciprocating Saw Blades (Hackzall)
notes: Keep metal and wood blades stocked separately.

name: Horizontal Bandsaw Blade (check stamped length)
notes: Blade lengths differ per saw and are stamped on the blade — read the old blade before ordering. 93-1/2" is the 14" vertical (Grizzly) length, not the 4×6 horizontal; the WEN BB4550 benchtop saw takes 44-7/8".

name: 2 AWG Tin-Plated Copper Lugs (1/4" hole)
notes: Battery/main-power lugs — single-crimp, use the hydraulic crimper.

name: Bussmann 120A Main Breakers
notes: FRC main breakers (Apr 2026 restock ×5).

name: Cable Zip Ties (12" 50 lb / 14" 120 lb)
notes: Jun 2026 restock (order WN60612912).

name: Slip-On Safety Side Shields (for prescription glasses)
location: PPE shelf by the shop door
notes: Makes prescription glasses pit-legal (Apr 2026).

name: Black Nitrile Exam Gloves
notes: For chemicals, powder, and finishing ONLY — never near rotating machinery.

name: Brother P-touch Label Tape (TZe, 12mm)
notes: Black on white, 12mm — the shop standard for bin labels.

name: NIIMBOT B1 Thermal Label Printer + Rolls
notes: Bluetooth app-driven, inkless thermal (Oct 2025). BETCKEY DYMO-compatible rolls $26.99 for the DYMO printers.

name: Evolution EVOMAX14ST 14" 80T Cermet Steel Blade
location: Mounted on the chop saw, or in its sleeve on the Orange Toolbox
notes: The steel blade. Cermet carbide, 1" arbor. Replace when cuts slow or the saw starts throwing sparks — a dry-cut saw making sparks has dead carbide. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Evolution EVOMAX14AL 14" 100T Aluminum Blade
location: Mounted on the chop saw, or in its sleeve on the Orange Toolbox
notes: The non-ferrous blade (bought July 2026). Rated to 1600 RPM — our ~1100 RPM saw is well inside it. Never cut steel with this blade.

name: 10" 60T ATB Fine-Finish Blade
notes: Wood, plywood and plastics. A 60T ATB gives clean edges in polycarbonate at moderate feed. Wood/plastics only — this saw never cuts metal. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: 93-1/2" Bandsaw Blade (Grizzly G0555)
notes: 93-1/2" is the G0555 length. Fine pitch (14–18 TPI) for aluminum, coarse skip-tooth for wood and plastic. Keep 3 teeth in the material. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: M12 Compact Band Saw Blades, 12/14 TPI
location: StackTech saw tower — Compact Bandsaw drawer
notes: 12/14 TPI is the general-purpose pitch and what the saw ships with. Thin-wall tube wants the finer 18 TPI. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: T-Shank Jig Saw Blade Assortment
location: StackTech power tower — Jigsaw & Nibbler drawer
notes: Fine-tooth blades for polycarbonate (coarse teeth chip and melt it). Blades are cheap; swap them instead of forcing a dull one. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: 3" Metal Cut-Off Wheels
location: StackTech power tower — Sanders & Cut-Off drawer
notes: Abrasive wheels shatter if twisted in the cut. Retire chipped or out-of-round wheels immediately. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Detail Sander Hook-and-Loop Pads
location: StackTech power tower — Sanders & Cut-Off drawer
notes: Work through grits. Replace pads when the grit polishes smooth — pressing harder on a dead pad just burns the workpiece. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: T50-Style 3/8" Crown Staples
notes: Bumper fabric and banner work. Match leg length to the material stack — too long and the point comes through the back of the plywood. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Carbide Turning Inserts (Oscarbide 1/2" set)
partNumber: Match the geometry printed on the holder box (CCMT / DCMT / TNMG / WNMG)
location: Lathe T-Stak — Indexable Turning Set & Inserts drawer
notes: The lathe runs an Oscarbide 7-piece 1/2" indexable set (SRDCN / SER / SVJCR / SCLCR / SWGCR / SDNCN / SDJCR). Order the insert style stamped on the holder — ask a mentor before switching geometry. Report chipped inserts, don't hide them. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: MGMN150-G Grooving / Parting Inserts (1.5 mm)
location: Lathe T-Stak — QCTP Holders & Setup drawer
notes: The narrow parting insert: a 1.5 mm kerf wastes less stock and needs less power, so it is the default for aluminum spacers and small-diameter work. Sold as a kit with its holder — buying the kit gets a spare holder you can leave pre-set in a QCTP block. (Amazon order, 15 Feb 2025.)

name: MGMN200-G Grooving / Parting Inserts (2 mm)
location: Lathe T-Stak — QCTP Holders & Setup drawer
notes: The wider, stiffer parting insert — the one for steel and for anything much over 1/2 in diameter. Every listing we bought these from (ApplianPar holder kit Feb 2023, ApplianPar 10-pack Jun 2022, an eBay 10-pack at $15.18) is now unavailable, but MGMN200-G is a generic ISO-style insert: any reputable seller's -G geometry drops into the MGEHR1212-2 holder. Do not order MGMN200-M or -H without asking a mentor — different chipbreaker, different feed.

name: Circlip Groove Inserts 16ER — 0.8 mm & 1.0 mm
location: Lathe T-Stak — QCTP Holders & Setup drawer
notes: The dedicated retaining-ring groove inserts — one width per ring size. 0.8 mm (0.0315 in) for 3/8 in rings, 1.0 mm (0.0394 in) for 1/2 in rings. Replaces the old practice of cutting ring grooves with the 1.5 mm parting insert, which left five times the axial slop. Ordered 22 Aug 2026, ETA ~11 Sep 2026 (one pack of each width). These are a shallow-groove grind in the 16ER threading-insert format — they are NOT parting tools. See /forming/lathe-snap-ring-grooves/.

name: SER1212H16 Insert Holders (circlip grooving)
location: Lathe T-Stak — QCTP Holders & Setup drawer
notes: External right-hand screw-clamp holders for the 16ER circlip groove inserts. Two were bought deliberately so each insert width lives in its own holder and its own pre-set QCTP block — 0.8 mm in one, 1.0 mm in the other, so nobody has to change an insert to change ring size. Same 12 mm shank as the MGEHR holders, so it drops into the same block. Screw clamp, not a spring clamp: it takes the T15 torx key, not the MGEHR L-key. Ordered 22 Aug 2026.

name: Dark Thread-Cutting Oil
notes: Steel tapping, threading and drilling. Aluminum runs dry, on WD-40, or on a wax stick. Powered tapping does NOT make dry aluminum safe to tap. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: #10-32 Spiral Point (Gun) Taps
location: Red toolbox drawer 7 (Thread Taps); one stays loaded in the tapping machine
notes: The shop's standing tap — the tapping machine keeps a #10-32 spiral point installed so the most common job needs zero setup. Spiral point pushes chips forward, so it is a through-hole tap; use spiral flute for blind holes. Tap drill: #21. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: 1/4-20 Spiral Point (Gun) Taps
notes: The other thread that runs the robot. Tap drill: #7. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: HSS Jobber Drill Bits (incl. #21 and #7)
location: StackTech hand tower — Drill Bits drawer; large bits in Orange Toolbox drawer 11
notes: The two number drills the team burns through are #21 and #7. Replace bits that squeal, smoke, or produce dust instead of chips — a dull bit is what grabs at breakthrough. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Center / Spotting Drills
notes: Start every tailstock hole and every precise drill-press hole with a center drill — it is the difference between a hole on your mark and a hole near it. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: ISO 68 Way Oil
notes: Wipe the ways and lay down a light film at close. Never blow chips off the ways with compressed air — it drives grit under the film. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: 1" × 30" Sanding Belts
location: Bench shelf by the belt sanders
notes: The 1×30 sander handles inside curves and detail work. Clean a glazed belt with a crepe stick before replacing it — aluminum loads belts long before it wears them out. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: 4" × 36" Sanding Belts
location: Bench shelf by the belt sanders
notes: Flats, squaring ends and chamfers. Same rule as the 1×30: crepe stick first, replace when the belt is bald or torn. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Scotch-Brite Deburring Wheel (6")
location: Fitted to the bench grinder; spares on the bench shelf
notes: Every sawed aluminum part visits this wheel. The wheel sheds rather than loads, which is why aluminum is allowed on it and never on the stone wheels. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: High-Temperature Polyester Masking Tape
notes: Blue painter's tape melts into goo at cure temperature. Mask threads, bearing seats and grounding points with this. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: High-Temp Silicone Plugs & Caps
partNumber: Tapered silicone plugs / pull plugs / caps
notes: Five plugs beat twenty inches of fiddly tape. Size them snug — powder finds loose plugs. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Furnace Filter for the Booth Box Fan
partNumber: Standard pleated furnace filter (match the fan)
notes: The filter is the booth's only filtration. Swap it when it is caked — checked weekly on the maintenance schedule. Measure the fan before ordering; sizes are not universal. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Bambu Hardened Steel Nozzle
notes: Filled filaments (PETG-GF, PPA-GF, CF nylon, PPS-CF) eat brass nozzles. The X1Cs run 0.6 mm and the H2D/X2D run 0.4 mm — order to match, and run a full calibration after any nozzle change. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Bambu Textured PEI Build Plate
notes: Textured PEI is the fleet-wide standard — one plate type across the farm. Replace a plate when the PEI is gouged bald; wash with Dawn and warm water long before that. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Prusa MINI Textured Powder-Coated Sheet
notes: Never clean a powder-coated sheet with acetone — it microfractures the texture. Dish soap and warm water only. Verify Live-Z after every sheet swap. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Prusa MINI Nozzle (0.6 mm)
notes: 0.6 mm is the farm standard. Hardened for anything filled; brass is fine for PLA and plain PETG. The MINI+ hotend is all-metal to 275 °C. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: HDPE Cleaning Filament
notes: Purge the hot end with this when stepping a nozzle DOWN in temperature — see Changing filaments on a nozzle in the Filament Guide. One roll on hand. Brand, price and reorder link are not recorded yet; more importantly, read the rated maximum temperature off the spool and add it here, because the purge procedure caps at the lower of the outgoing material's temperature and this filament's ceiling, and most HDPE is rated short of PPA-GF's 310 °C.

name: PINECIL Soldering Tips (TS/B2, C4, K)
notes: B2 conical for general work, C4 chisel for wire and lugs, K knife for drag soldering. A dead tip is usually an un-tinned tip — tin before parking the iron. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: 63/37 Rosin-Core Solder + Flux Pen
notes: 63/37 is eutectic — it goes solid instantly instead of through a slushy stage, which is what makes cold joints. Flux is not optional on anything oxidised. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Adhesive-Lined Heat Shrink Assortment
notes: Adhesive-lined for battery lugs and anything that flexes — heat until adhesive beads at both ends. Shrink it with the DeWalt heat gun on LOW. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: Simple Green All-Purpose Cleaner
notes: Spectrum's standard degreaser for drivetrain parts, chain and gears. Spray on the rag, not the robot. Do NOT use it on polycarbonate you want to stay clear — it clouds the appearance (soap and water for polycarb). From the team [maintenance guide](https://spectrum3847.org/resources/maintenance-guide/).

name: Tri-Flow Superior Lubricant
location: StackTech hand tower — Grease & Loctite drawer
notes: The team's planetary and chain lubricant: a few drops on each gear, a few drops on the sprockets. Not a substitute for gearbox lube — see WD-40 PTFE dry spray for that. From the team [maintenance guide](https://spectrum3847.org/resources/maintenance-guide/).

name: WD-40 Specialist Dry Lube with PTFE
location: StackTech hand tower — Grease & Loctite drawer
notes: Gearbox lubrication: spray in while rotating the gearbox so every tooth gets coated. Dry film, so it does not collect the grit that wet lube does. From the team [maintenance guide](https://spectrum3847.org/resources/maintenance-guide/).

name: Loctite 242/243 Blue Threadlocker (gel) — backup
location: StackTech hand tower — Grease & Loctite drawer
notes: Works, and there is some on the shelf, but the shop's first choice is the Vibra-Tite 125 gel above. Never on polycarbonate/Lexan, ABS or acrylic; nylon and Delrin are fine.

name: Blue Shop Towels
notes: Stronger than paper towels and disposable — the right rag for grease and cutting oil. Microfibre cloths for wheels, rollers and anything you want to stay clean. (list estimate — no receipt on file; update the price when we next order).

name: ENGINEER PZ-58 Screw Removal Pliers
notes: Removes stripped 10-32 button heads by gripping the outside of the head. Needs real grip strength — often easier for an adult than a student. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: KNIPEX Snap Ring Pliers
notes: Better than the cheaper snap-ring pliers we tried: the tips do not bend, they hold the ring, and they open around a hex shaft. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: VESSEL 400ER3 Electric Slim Ratchet
notes: USB-C powered, head barely bigger than a manual ratchet, so it reaches into the robot and turns a bolt where there is no swing room. Niche, but it makes some repairs 10x faster. We own two. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: Wera Joker 3/8" Ratcheting Combination Wrench
notes: The jaw holds a nut while you start it — worth it the first time it saves you three minutes on a hard-to-reach bolt in the pit. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: 1/4" Hex Bits, 5/32" and 1/8"
location: Red toolbox drawer 10; StackTech Allen Wrenches drawer
notes: Buy a pile. 5/32" drives 10-32 socket head, 1/8" drives 10-32 button and flat. Having them loose for torque drivers, drills and impacts is what makes torquing to spec actually happen. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: NIIMBOT D110 Mini Label Maker
notes: Small Bluetooth label printer for robot parts, wires and tool locations. Cheap enough that there is no excuse for an unlabelled anything. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: CRC Plastic Safe Contact Cleaner
notes: The shop's general-purpose cleaner: robot electronics, silicone rollers (it is plastic-safe, which most contact cleaners are not), and general dust and debris — it lifts grime so it wipes up. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: Vibra-Tite 125 Removable Threadlocker Gel
location: StackTech hand tower — Grease & Loctite drawer
notes: "By far our favourite thread locker." The gel applies far more cleanly than the liquid bottles and does not dry out like the glue-stick kind. We stock medium and high strength. Never on polycarbonate, Lexan, ABS or acrylic. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: Sea to Summit Hook Release Accessory Straps
notes: Battery retention straps. Very secure, cut to any length, and they pass through a 1/2" drilled hole — which is what makes them good for getting through inspection. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: WISEUP Magnetic Tape Measure (fractions + metric)
notes: Imperial fractions for shop work and metric for measuring out auton paths, on one tape. Magnetic tip. Durable for the price — we own six or eight. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.

name: M12 Band File Belts
notes: Belts for the M12 band file — the tool that sands parts already bolted to the robot, in spaces no other sander reaches. Faster than hand-filing and a pit favourite. Picked out in Spectrum's own review of a year of tool and supply purchases as one of the items worth the price.
